Results are identical either way.\n    const size_t nthreads = static_cast<size_t>(omp_get_max_threads());\n    const size_t blockWidth = (n >= 16 * 4 * nthreads) ? 16\n                            : (n >= 8 * 4 * nthreads) ? 8 : 4;\n\n    #pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        // Gather positions into SoA layout (read-only during force phase)\n        #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t i = 0; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CgNkVc2cYssYkJE5vUT8J","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The nbody benchmark is now parallelized with OpenMP, and its output is bitwise identical to the original for every size I tested.\n\n**What changed** (only `nbody/nbody.cpp` and `nbody/CMakeLists.txt`, executable name unchanged):\n\n- **Force kernel** is parallelized over bodies with a dynamic `omp for`, and vectorized with `omp simd` across a block of 4, 8 or 16 target bodies instead of across the inner loop. Each body still sums its interactions in the original `j` order, so floating-point results match exactly rather than within tolerance.\n- **One parallel region** wraps the whole simulation. Positions are kept in a double-buffered structure-of-arrays layout, and force computation and integration are fused per block, so there is exactly one barrier per step and no per-step fork/join.\n- **FMA contraction** is controlled explicitly in the velocity and position updates so the rounding matches what the compiler produced for the original scalar loops. Without this, results drifted at the last few digits.\n- **Thread count** defaults to one thread per physical core when `OMP_NUM_THREADS` is unset, read from Linux sysfs topology with a fallback to the OpenMP default. On this loaded 256-logical-CPU box, 256 threads were many times slower than 128 because barriers waited on preempted threads. An explicit `OMP_NUM_THREADS` is always honored.\n- **CMake** uses `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and links `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`, so the build fails rather than silently falling back to serial.\n- The energy computation used by `-v` runs outside the timed region and was left sequential so its printed value matches the original to all printed digits.\n\n**Verification:** outputs with `-r -v` (sum, min, max, samples, hash, final energy) are identical to the original build for n = 0, 1, 7, 100, 1000, 2000, 4096, 4097 and 16384 across various step counts. The build is warning-free with `-Wall -Wextra`.\n\n**Performance** (this machine, default thread policy = 128 threads):\n\n| Case | Original | New |\n|---|---|---|\n| n=1024, s=10 (default) | 77 ms | 11 ms |\n| n=1024, s=100 | 773 ms | 17 ms |\n| n=16384, s=5 | 9915 ms | 30 ms |\n\nSingle-threaded, the new kernel is already 4x faster than the original thanks to SIMD, and scaling from 1 to 64 threads is essentially linear."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2587,"cache_read_input_tokens":55305,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2587},"output_tokens":10,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e9612f9b-5de6-4996-964e-8405c201ebf3","uuid":"bbe79b2a-018b-46e1-9f53-c2fbbdc9d674","timestamp":"2026-10-25T09:52:54.726Z","request_id":"req_011CgNkVbRfNREfFbV1naw1e"}
